LESSON: HUMAN RIGHTS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Development and Governance
Topic 5.3: Human Rights
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Human Rights, part of Political Development and Governance in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to know our rights? 2. How can we promote equity and non- discrimination in society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Human Rights together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: Learners develop social and civic skills as they participate in commemorating the International Day for

the Elimination of Racial Discrimination.

● Creativity and Imagination: Learners make connections between what was learnt in class and exchange new ideas

that inspire creative thinking as they create posters on the classification of human rights.

Values:
● Social justice: Learners advocate for harmonious relationships in the society as they develop posters on equity and

non-discrimination.

● Unity: Learners collaborate with others as they create posters on the classification and use a tree diagram to indicate

characteristics of human rights.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Social Cohesion: Learners develop harmonious coexistence as they participate in commemorating International Day

for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination on 21st March.

● Good Governance: Learners develop posters on equity and non- discrimination and display them in school

Link to other subjects:

● Creative Arts: Learners develop posters on equity and non- discrimination and display them in school.

73

● Religious Education: Learners brainstorm issues of equity and non-discrimination.

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Resource persons, digital resources with assistive technology, approved textbooks and other printed or braille

resources, embossed/ tactile charts, posters, flip charts / manila papers and a copy of The Constitution of Kenya.
